info.title: agentsfleet Control Plane API
info.description: API for managing workspaces, fleets, triggers, and runs.

get.description: Returns 200 as long as the process is alive and able to serve HTTP. Does not probe dependencies — use /readyz for readiness (database + queue).
Returns 200 when the database and event queue are available, and 503 when either is not. Never shed: an orchestrator that cannot reach this because the instance is busy learns nothing it can act on.

get.summary: List the platform Fleet library catalog
get.description: Lists every entry in the global platform catalog. Published, draft, and entries whose bundle was never fetched all appear. Unlike the workspace gallery, this operator view hides nothing: it shows what is live and what still needs work. Requires the `platform- library:write` scope. Metadata only — never bundle markdown, a support-file body, or an object-store key. Each row carries an `etag` that an editor can send as `If-Match` on PATCH.

patch.summary: Curate, publish, or unpublish a platform Fleet library entry
patch.description: Partial update. `description` and `required_credentials_reasons` are the two fields no bundle can supply, so they are operator-owned: a later bundle refetch never overwrites them. `published` moves the entry between `draft` (stored, invisible to every tenant) and `public` (live in every workspace gallery and installable). Publishing an entry whose bundle was never fetched is refused — a published entry always has something to install. Requires the `platform-library:write` scope. Send `If-Match` with the row's `etag` to reject stale edits before they can repoint the source or unpublish the entry. Omitting the header preserves last-write-wins behavior.

post.description: Checks the six-digit code and returns encrypted sign-in data. The code can be used once. A retry from the same client within 60 seconds returns the same response. Later retries return 410 `UZ- AUTH-012`. `UZ-AUTH-011` means the code did not match. The fifth failed attempt ends the session. `UZ-AUTH-018` means the code was not six digits. `UZ-AUTH-013` means the session ended. `UZ-AUTH-014` means approval is pending. `UZ-AUTH-006` means the session expired after 5 minutes.

patch.description: Platform-admin mutation on a single runner. The body carries exactly one of `action` or `assigned_policy`. `action` moves the admin state: `cordon` to cordoned, `drain` to draining, `revoke` to revoked. Revoked is terminal; a revoked runner cannot transition back. `self_test` moves no state. It records a request for the runner to test its own sandbox. The host picks the request up on its next heartbeat and answers on a later one. The reply is the recorded request, never a verdict. A revoked runner refuses it with 409 `UZ- RUN-018`, since it will never heartbeat again. `assigned_policy` re- assigns the runner's policy, and the host picks it up on its next heartbeat. Sending the same policy again changes nothing and records no event.

get.description: Platform-admin read of a single runner's lease history, newest first. Each lease is joined to its Fleet event, so outcome and failure cause arrive in one round trip. Stripe-style keyset pagination — `starting_after` is a lease id from a previous page's `next_cursor`. Settled leases are retained for 30 days. The window is measured from settlement, not from acquisition. A lease acquired long ago and settled yesterday keeps its full window. A background sweep deletes them past that window. A lease still running or renewing is never swept. The per-lease activity records (`lease_acquired`, `lease_released`) are swept on the same 30-day window. Each record ages from when it occurred, not from its lease's settlement. A long run's opening record can therefore be pruned shortly before its lease row. The runner's lifecycle activity is kept at any age, so a long-lived runner's feed never empties. A lease whose runner died without reporting is marked expired once it passes the same window. It then keeps its own window, like any settled lease. The lifetime totals on `GET /v1/fleets/runners/{id}` are unaffected by any of this. They count transitions as they happen, not surviving rows. A long-lived runner's `leases_acquired` will therefore exceed what this endpoint returns.

get.description: Returns models available to the tenant. Each item includes its provider, context limit, and usage fields. An empty library returns an empty array. A bounded keyset page ordered by normalized `model_id`, then normalized `provider`, then an opaque row identity. Every comparison runs under `COLLATE "C"`, so the order is byte-wise and stable across locales. Follow `next_cursor` to read the whole catalogue; a client that reads only the first page silently loses every model past it. The response is conditionally revalidated. Every answer carries an `ETag` over the exact bytes served, plus `Cache-Control: private, no-cache` and `Vary: Authorization`. Send the tag back as `If-None-Match` and a match answers `304` with no body and the same headers. `private` is what stops a shared proxy handing one tenant's response to another even though the payload is identical for every authorized caller.

get.summary: Stream live activity for a whole workspace
get.description: Opens ONE Server-Sent Events (SSE) stream carrying live activity for every fleet the caller can read in the workspace. It is the Fleets Wall's single connection, replacing one stream per tile. The first frame is `event: hello`. Its `data` is `{"kind":"hello","fleet_ids":[...]}` for the current readable fleet set. Activity frame `data` contains the publisher payload with `fleet_id` added as the leading field. The client routes each frame by that tag. A stalled client can overflow its bounded server queue. The server then sends `event: catching_up` with `{"kind":"catching_up","dropped":N}`. `dropped` is the new drop count since the previous signal. Control frames use identifier 0 and do not advance the activity sequence. Activity identifiers start at 0 for each connection. The route ignores `Last-Event-ID`. The connection adjusts its fan-in as fleets appear or disappear. A caller whose workspace access is revoked stops receiving on the next refresh. At capacity the route returns 503 `UZ-API-002` with `Retry- After`. After a reconnect opens, recover the gap through `GET /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/events`.

did not come across in the port: `public/openapi.json` declares this GET and

this fleet does not hold.

One event as the operator surface renders it.

Field order is load-bearing. `events.zig` hands its `EventRow` straight to
`res.json(value, .{})`, which emits the struct's field set in DECLARATION
order, and the tenant parity suite pins key set AND order — a reordering that a
set comparison would call identical is one a client reading ordered columns
can feel. So this declaration mirrors `fleet_events_store.zig`'s `EventRow`
field for field.

Every optional stays on the wire as an explicit `null` rather than being
skipped, which is this crate's rule everywhere and the reason it declares no
`skip_serializing_if`: the Zig emitter writes `null` for an absent optional,
so a dropped key would be a byte mismatch against the daemon still serving.

workspace's own. Opaque to a caller either way.

required_credentials_reasons.description:
Per-credential "why this fleet needs it" copy, keyed by name.

An empty object for a workspace's own entry: that library derives no
reasons, and the read projects `{}` rather than a null so a client has
one shape to render for both tiers.

requirements.description: Credential, tool and host names. Never values.

source_ref.description: The repository or template it was onboarded from.

visibility.description: Which library the card came from: `platform` or `tenant`.

items.description: The cards, newest first, platform before tenant within an instant.

next_cursor.description: Where the next page resumes, or null on the last one.

total.description:
Always null.

Counting a keyset page costs the scan the pagination exists to avoid,
and §3 declares null to mean "not computed" rather than letting the key
vanish from the envelope.

GrantSummary.description:
One grant as the fleet's list shows it.

`approved_at` and `revoked_at` are the two instants a grant's own
transitions stamp — the table carries no `updated_at`, because a row-change
time would say nothing those two do not already say. Both are `null` on a
pending row and exactly one is set afterwards.

approved_at.description: When a person approved it, or `null`.

id.description: The grant's own row id — what a revoke addresses it by.

reason.description: Why the row exists at all — the install's own words, stored once.

revoked_at.description: When a person took that back, or `null`.

service.description: The third party the grant is about, as the credential classifier names it.

GrantsResponse.description:
`GET /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/fleets/{fleet_id}/integration-grants`.

`total` is the length of `items` and not a count of everything stored: the
list is unpaged, because a fleet holds at most one grant per service and the
supported-service count is what bounds it. Emitted anyway, because the Zig
handler emits it and a dashboard reads it.

name.description: The name it was stored under — the drawn one, when a default collided.

status.description: Where it stands. `active`: the stream exists, so it is already leasable.

webhook_urls.description:
One entry per webhook trigger the bundle declared, keyed by source.

An empty object where the fleet declares none, never `null`: a client
iterating the map should not have to branch on its absence first.

MemoriesResponse.description:
`GET /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/fleets/{fleet_id}/memories` — one page.

Exactly three fields, and an integration test pins the count: a page that
grew a fourth would be a shape the dashboard's parser did not agree to.

items.description: The entries on this page, newest first.

next_cursor.description: Where the next page resumes, or `null` on the last one.

total.description:
How many are on THIS page — not the fleet's whole count. The name is
the one that shipped, and `handler.zig` answers the page length too.

MemoryCaptureResponse.description:
`POST /v1/runners/me/memory/{fleet_id}` reply — what the write did.

A runner acts on both numbers: `stored` says its memory landed, `skipped`
says some was refused for shape and it should look at what it sends. The
sweep and eviction counts the control plane also computes stay in the log —
they are the daemon's housekeeping, not a fact about this request.

Declared here rather than assembled inline at the handler, which is where it
used to live. The argument for inline was that no `wire-v2` fixture pins
this shape, so a type would claim a frozen contract the corpus does not
carry. That confuses two things: `tests/roundtrip.rs` generates its cases
from an explicit fixture ROSTER, so a type absent from that roster is
pinned by nothing and claims nothing. What the inline version did claim was
that a response body could be spelled somewhere other than this crate, and
two keys written by hand at a call site are two keys nothing type-checks.

skipped.description: Deltas refused for shape, which the runner should investigate.

MemoryDelta.description:
One durable memory item — the unit of both capture and hydrate.

Carries no scope: the fleet is a path segment, validated server-side against
the runner's live lease.

category.description: Retention category, which decides eviction order.

key.description: Stable key. A repeated key overwrites rather than accumulating.

MemoryEntry.description:
One stored entry as the OPERATOR surface renders it.

A [`MemoryDelta`] plus the instant it was last written. The runner's two
verbs carry no timestamp — a fleet being seeded with what it knows has no
use for one — while a person reading the list is deciding whether a lesson
is still current, which is the whole question `updated_at` answers.

Field order is load-bearing. `memory/handler.zig` hands its `MemoryEntry`
straight to `res.json`, which emits the struct's fields in DECLARATION
order, and a dashboard diffing two responses byte-for-byte would see a
reorder as a change.

category.description: The retention category, which decides eviction order.

key.description: The stable key the fleet remembers this under.

updated_at.description: Epoch milliseconds, as a JSON NUMBER — never a decimal string.

expires_at_ms.description:
Epoch milliseconds after which it stops working, so the caller re-mints
before expiry rather than on failure.

token.description:
The short-lived, workspace-scoped credential. Secret — never logged,
never echoed into a frame.

ModelRates.description: Mutable rate fields shared by admin model create and patch.

NetworkPolicy.description: Egress posture assigned per runner, named so the behaviour reads off the value.

OnboardingResponse.description:
`GET /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/onboarding` — the whole checklist.

Five derived signals and three preference reads in one call, which is the
consolidation this endpoint exists for: the dashboard used to fetch it as
six separate requests.

Eight booleans, and `struct_excessive_bools` is right that this usually
means a missing type. Not here: this IS the wire shape, field for field, and
the dashboard destructures all eight. Collapsing any of them into an enum
would change the JSON a shipped client reads.

cli_ticked.description: The person ticked the install-the-CLI step by hand.

collapsed.description: The panel is collapsed but not dismissed.

dismissed.description: The person dismissed the panel outright.

has_fleet.description: The workspace holds at least one fleet.

has_processed_event.description: At least one event has reached the workspace.

has_secret.description: The workspace holds at least one vault secret.

has_steer_event.description: At least one of those events came from a steer.

model_configured.description: A model resolves — the tenant's own selection, or the platform default.

oneOf.description: An empty body: nothing was written, and no row was even read.

config_revision.description:
Always `null` — the literal `@as(?i64, null)` the Zig answers, kept
because a client distinguishes "no write" from a revision by it.

oneOf.description: A configuration or source edit, with no transition asked for.

config_revision.description: The new revision — `updated_at`, echoed back by a conditional caller.

etag.description: The tag over the post-update source, for the editor's next save.

oneOf.description: A transition, with or without an edit beside it.

etag.description: The tag over the post-update source.

PatchedFleetResponse.description:
What a PATCH answers with — one of three shapes, as `patch.zig` writes them.

An untagged enum rather than one struct with optional keys, and that is the
rule this crate already keeps rather than an exception to it: no
`skip_serializing_if` appears here, because each variant emits exactly the
keys its case carries. A config-only edit never wrote a `status` key, and a
no-op never wrote an `etag` — with one struct those would have to be skipped
conditionally, which is the thing that silently drops a field somebody adds
later.

It also makes two impossible responses impossible: an `etag` without a
revision, and a revision on the no-op.

PollSessionResponse.description:
`GET /v1/auth/sessions/{session_id}` — where a login has got to.

Never carries ciphertext. The poll is unauthenticated — the id is the only
thing presented — so anything it returns is readable by whoever holds the
id, and the sealed credential is released only by `/verify`, against a code
that never travelled the same channel.

cli_public_key.description: The public key the command line presented, echoed back.

expires_at_ms.description: When the window closes, in milliseconds since the epoch.

token_name.description: What the credential will be called.

ProviderMode.description:
The `mode` a client sends and reads back.

Two spellings and no third, so a body naming something else is refused by
serde at the boundary rather than by a string comparison inside a handler.

RenewResponse.description:
`POST /v1/runners/me/leases/{lease_id}/renew` reply.

The authoritative new kill deadline. A non-`200` means stop renewing and kill
the child — the run is over.

lease_expires_at.description: Epoch milliseconds of the new deadline.

ResolvedResponse.description: What answering a gate reports, whether or not this caller won the race.

resolved_by.description: Who decided it — not necessarily this caller.

active.description:
Always `false` — the field is present so a client can write the reply
straight into whatever it was holding.

revoked_at.description: When the row records it stopped working.

oneOf.description: The assignment as stored, on the policy-update path.

selftest_requested_at.description:
When the self-test request was recorded, epoch milliseconds.

The reply is the REQUEST, never a verdict — the daemon picks the ask up
on its next beat, so a result cannot exist yet. Returning the instant
lets a reader age the pending state instead of spinning with no clock.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page, or null at the end.

RunnerItem.description: One runner in the newest-first operator list.

oneOf.description: Capability report most recently supplied by the host.
Policy currently assigned to the host.

degraded.description: Whether the assignment exceeds the reported capability.

degraded_reason.description: Stored explanation for a degraded verdict.

host_id.description: Stable host identity supplied at enrolment.

last_seen_at.description: Last heartbeat instant in epoch milliseconds.

liveness.description: Runtime state derived from heartbeat and leases.

RunnerLiveness.description:
Derived runtime liveness, computed by the fleet read and NEVER stored —
storing it would drift from the values it is derived from.

RunnersResponse.description: A keyset page of runner list rows.

next_cursor.description: Cursor to send as `starting_after` on the next request.

total.description: Total runner rows independent of the boundary.

SandboxTier.description:
Isolation strength the control plane assigns. Only tiers with real
enforcement are members: a tier that cannot be applied must not be assignable.

SecretSummary.description:
One credential as the list shows it.

`model` is documented as optional in `SecretSummary` and is not emitted:
`vault.secrets` has no column for it, and answering it would mean decrypting
every row on a page that displays no secrets. See `afd_vault::projection`.

base_url.description: The custom endpoint, where one may be displayed.

created_at.description: When it was first stored, in epoch milliseconds.

kind.description: The server's classification. A client reads this and never re-derives it.

name.description: The name the secret is stored and interpolated under.

provider.description: The provider label, for the kinds that carry one.

SelfResponse.description:
`GET /v1/runners/me` reply — the runner's own registration row, read-only.

Reading this does NOT bump liveness, so inspecting a host can never mask a
dead runner.

oneOf.description: What the host reported it can actually enforce.
The policy currently assigned to it.

last_seen_at.description: Epoch milliseconds of the last beat; zero when never seen.

StoredSecretResponse.description:
What a create and a replace both answer with.

One shape for both verbs because both say the same thing — which name now
holds a secret — and the status code is what distinguishes them.

name.description: The name the secret is stored under.

TenantProviderResponse.description: `GET /v1/tenants/me/provider`, and what a write answers with.

context_cap_tokens.description: The context window the catalogue prices this model at.

mode.description: Whose key this tenant's runs dial with.

model.description: The model identifier as the provider spells it.

platform_default_available.description:
Whether an active platform-default row exists at all.

Independent of this tenant's own mode, so the Models page can gate its
"Switch to Default" action BEFORE the click rather than after a failed
write.

provider.description: The provider the model belongs to.

secret_ref.description:
The credential dialled under self-managed mode.

Omitted rather than null under platform mode: an absent field and a
null one are read differently by enough clients that the wire should
carry only one of them, and the daemon's own logfmt rule already says
absent.

ThreadResponse.description:
A page of one fleet's chat thread, bodies included.

The sibling of [`EventsResponse`], and it carries [`EventDetail`] where
that carries [`EventSummary`]: the chat view needs the newest turns WITH
their payload and answer, and used to fan out one detail request per turn
to get them.

# `total` is always null, and is on the wire anyway

`messages_list.zig` writes `.total = null` and has never written anything
else — the count would cost a second statement per page for a number the
view does not render. Dropping the key would be a byte mismatch against
the daemon still serving, so it stays, typed as the count it would hold.

items.description: The turns on this page, newest first.

next_cursor.description: Where the next page resumes, or `null` when this one ends the walk.

total.description: How many turns the thread holds in total. Never populated.

VerifySessionResponse.description:
What a redeemed login hands back.

Identical for a first redemption and for a repeat inside the replay window,
deliberately: a command line asking again after a dropped connection must
not be able to learn that its first request landed.

nonce.description: The nonce it was sealed under.

WebhookUrl.description: Where one declared webhook trigger is delivered.

url.description: The address it posts to, on this deployment.

WorkspaceSummary.description: One workspace as the list shows it.

created_at.description: When it was created; the walk's sort key.

name.description:
Its name — `null` on rows older than naming, emitted either way for
the tenant module's null rule.

WorkspacesResponse.description: `GET /v1/tenants/me/workspaces` — one page of the tenant's workspaces.

items.description: The rows on this page, oldest first.

next_cursor.description: Where the next page resumes, or `null` on the last page.

tenant_id.description:
Whose list this is — the authoritative resolution, carried so a client
can pin its local state to the right tenant.

total.description:
Always `null`: the walk never counts, and the key stays because a
client may already branch on its presence.

BearerAuth.description: Obtain a token via the CLI auth flow (POST /v1/auth/sessions) or GitHub OAuth
